newsitem.title: USA: NYCE cotton called to open little changed.
newsitem.headline: NYCE cotton called to open little changed.

text.p: NYCE cotton futures were called to open little changed on Tuesday, based on market orders at 1018 EST, dealers said.
New York cotton futures finished firmer Monday in dull, rangebound dealings. March cotton settled 0.41 cent firmer at 74.18 cents per pound, traded 74.30 to 73.45 cents.
Volume Monday reached an estimated at 9,557 lots compared with Friday's 9,187 lots.

Traders said the spec/hedge report released this morning showed speculators were about 9 percent net short. With recent bouts of fund selling, traders had anticipated the report to show speculators 8 to 13 percent net short.
"Basically it was what everyone expected," one trader said.

In fundamental news, Aegean Exporters Union officials said on Tuesday Turkey's cotton exports since the export season began in September 1996 reached 37,208 tonnes to January 10 and earned it $52.8 million.

No comparison was available for the same period in the previous 1995/96 harvest year, they said, but Turkey exported a total of 58,465 tonnes in the 1995/96 export season (Sept-Aug), when its exports were limited to a quota of 100,000 tonnes. The government later abolished the quota.
Elsewhere, Turkmenistan produced 270,500 tonnes of cotton fibre in the January-November 1996 period, down 4.3 percent on year-earlier levels, the State Statistics Committee said on Tuesday.
